questions.prompt: Why is the mitochondrion called the powerhouse of the cell?
options: It turns food into usable energy for the cell
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion breaks down food molecules using oxygen and releases the energy as usable ATP, which powers the cell's work.
questions.misconception: Storage of instructions is the nucleus's job; making energy from food is specifically the mitochondrion's role.

questions.prompt: Why does the inner membrane of the mitochondrion have folds (cristae)?
options: To create more surface area for making energy
To store water for the cell
questions.explanation: The folds give the inner membrane a much larger surface area, so many of the cell's energy machines can fit and produce ATP quickly.
questions.misconception: Folds are not for storage or warmth - they are about surface area, the same trick used to fit more work into a small space.

options: The usable energy molecule the cell spends
The protein that makes up muscles
questions.explanation: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the small molecule the cell stores energy in and then spends to power its activities.
questions.misconception: ATP is not food or muscle - it is the 'energy coin' that carries energy from where it is made to where it is used.

questions.prompt: Why does the body need to breathe oxygen?
options: Mitochondria need oxygen to release energy from food efficiently
questions.explanation: Cells release the most energy from food when they have oxygen; the oxygen is used in cellular respiration inside the mitochondria.
questions.misconception: We don't breathe to cool down or to feed bones. The deep reason is energy - oxygen helps mitochondria release energy efficiently.

questions.prompt: Which type of cell would you expect to contain the most mitochondria?
questions.explanation: Cells that work hardest need the most energy, so muscle cells pack in many mitochondria, sometimes thousands.
questions.misconception: Mitochondria are not spread evenly - high-energy cells (muscle, brain) are packed with them, low-energy cells have fewer.
